title: Comparison of conventional corneal crosslinking with the accelerated procedure in progressive keratoconus

groups.description: Standard-protocol corneal cross-linking (S-CXL, 3 mW/cm2 for 30 min) for progressive keratoconus; retrospective cohort enrolled 2009-2013, one eye per patient (Tab1!R3C2). Two standard protocols compared without an investigational arm, so both groups are control.
Accelerated-protocol corneal cross-linking (A-CXL, 9 mW/cm2 for 10 min) for progressive keratoconus; retrospective cohort enrolled 2009-2013, one eye per patient (Tab1!R3C3).

exclusions.reason: the same baseline of the same groups as Table 5; cited from Table 5 only, used here only to establish the unit

exclusions.what: Fig. 4 (mean change from baseline of visual acuity) and Fig. 5 (categorized change of visual acuity)
exclusions.reason: figure values and line-change categories are not admissible (protocol inclusion 4); the tabulated means of Table 5 are used

notes: Methods: 'Best-corrected visual acuity was determined'; it is the only acuity measure reported, and the only acuity unit the article states is logMAR (Table 1).

Inclusion was restricted to subjects whose measurements were all performed with the same Pentacam device (to avoid a device change; the authors say this explains the smaller S-CXL group). This is a measurement criterion defined by the device, not a postoperative-outcome or complete-follow-up selection: losses to follow-up remain in the groups.

Attrition (Complications section): S-CXL, 4 eyes required CXL retreatment for progression and 2 patients were lost to follow-up (at 3 and 8 years); A-CXL, 5 eyes required repeat CXL, 2 eyes underwent further procedures (alcohol keratectomy, DMEK) and were excluded from subsequent follow-up, and 16 patients were lost to follow-up between 3 and 8 years. Whether visits after a repeat CXL were retained is not stated. Per-visit n is not reported; kept as ordinary attrition with this note.
Longitudinal tests used a linear mixed model with Bonferroni correction; Table 5 prints descriptive mean ± SD (95% CI of the mean), not model-adjusted estimates.
Tomography (Kmean, Kmax, ARC, PRC, ISV, IVA, TCT, CCT; Table 2), corneal densitometry (Table 3) and higher-order aberrations (Table 4) are tabulated; not extracted (no such series in schema 1.0.0).
Supplement 1 (CXL settings, DOCX) is not acquired for this dataset.
combined = null: the article neither states nor explicitly rules out same-session cataract surgery (addendum 1, point 3).

series.baseline_label: Baseline best-corrected visual acuity, S-CXL row (Table 5)
series.notes: Cells print mean ± SD (95% CI of the mean); the leading mean is read. Table 5 (best-corrected visual acuity) prints no unit; the article states the unit of this visual acuity variable as logMAR in Table 1 ('visual acuity (logMAR)', Tab1!R7), whose baseline cell for this group has the same text as Tab5!R3C3. Times are the stated visits (baseline, 6, 12, 36 and 96 months). Per-visit n not reported; n is the number of eyes at baseline.
